hidden_dual_route_1.name: {name}
hidden_dual_route_1.text: *My feet stop in front of the school gate. The envelope presses against my chest, and the bandage on my hand catches on my sleeve.*

hidden_dual_route_choice.name: {name}
hidden_dual_route_choice.text: *My hand stops between the envelope and the bandage.*
choices: Go to the person who handed me the manuscript
Go to the person who left an answer on the back of my hand

perfect_seo_1.name: {name}
perfect_seo_1.text: *Seoyeon's rooftop. Standing among the plants she grew herself.*

perfect_seo_1_b.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_1_b.text: *Her eyes are wet. This time, she does not hide them with the back of her hand.*

perfect_seo_2.name: {name}
perfect_seo_2.text: *Her eyes are completely wet. Even so, she doesn't look away.*

perfect_seo_3.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_3.text: ...Even when you have this face, don't run away.

perfect_seo_4.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_4.text: *The rooftop breeze stirs around us.* Even after graduation, I'll keep coming here. These plants only really grow when you're here.

perfect_seo_5.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_5.text: *She reaches out. Not a pinky finger. Her whole hand.*

perfect_epilogue_1_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_seo.text: *I walked the same path every morning. Next to Seoyeon, the same road had a different expression every time.*

perfect_epilogue_2_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_seo.text: *University entrance ceremony day. A message on my phone. 'Watered the plant today. — But come home soon.'*

perfect_epilogue_3_seo.name: Seoyeon
perfect_epilogue_3_seo.text: *She doesn't delete photos even when her eyeliner has smudged a little. The cotton pads in front of the mirror haven't been used once today.*

bitter_seo_1.name: {name}
bitter_seo_1.text: *I confessed. Seoyeon said let's try. A month or so later, she messaged asking to meet at the café in front of school. The message ended with only a period.*

bitter_seo_2.name: Seoyeon
bitter_seo_2.text: ...I thought we'd be fine. I guess you and I are both one step late.

bitter_seo_2_b.name: {name}
bitter_seo_2_b.text: *Seoyeon at the café. Her gaze stays on the coaster behind her glasses. The coffee she ordered is barely half gone.*

bitter_seo_3.name: {name}
bitter_seo_3.text: *I left the cafe. It's raining. We used to share one umbrella — now we each have our own.*

true_seo_1.name: {name}
true_seo_1.text: *Seoyeon's room. Her parents are out. Items on the desk are aligned as if measured with a ruler, and the family photo in the frame is tilted slightly.*

true_seo_2.name: {name}
true_seo_2.text: *— Except for one thing. On the desk, a row of plants Seoyeon grew herself.*

true_seo_3.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_3.text: In front of you, I think I do not need the practiced face.

true_seo_5.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_5.text: ...know. But it took some time to believe it.

true_seo_6.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_6.text: *She smiles. Her hair scatters in the wind.*

true_seo_6b.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_6b.text: I always had to smile. With you, I just want to be myself.

true_seo_7_b.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_7_b.text: *She hesitates, then holds out her pinky.*

true_seo_7b.name: {name}
true_seo_7b.text: *I reach out too. Just before our fingers touch, Seoyeon smiles first.*

true_seo_8.name: {name}
true_seo_8.text: *We linked pinkies. The finger that cut through empty air on the first day is now hooked around mine.*

true_seo_bridge.name: {name}
true_seo_bridge.text: *The promise Seoyeon gave me still lingers in my hand.*

true_epilogue_1_seo.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_seo.text: *It was five days. Until I saw the face Seoyeon had hidden behind her clipboard.*

perfect_yuna_1.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_1.text: *The library annex, the secret attic. Yuna hands over a short story.*

perfect_yuna_2.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_2.text: *The title is the main character's name.*

perfect_yuna_3.name: Yuna
perfect_yuna_3.text: ...Tell me what you think after you finish it. That's my answer.

perfect_yuna_4.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_4.text: *The last sentence of the story: 'There was someone who did not disappear.' The ink blurs a little beneath it.*

perfect_yuna_5.name: Yuna
perfect_yuna_5.text: *She stood and hugged me. Without a word. Light from the broken window stretched long across the floor. Her hand stopped slowly behind my back.*

perfect_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *I sat in the same place every day. The sound of Yuna turning the pages was also slightly different every day.*

perfect_epilogue_2_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_yuna.text: *Yuna's debut novel was published. The dedication: 'To the third star.'*

perfect_epilogue_3_yuna.name: Yuna
perfect_epilogue_3_yuna.text: *She is still quiet. But only with {name}, her sentences have grown longer.*

bitter_yuna_1.name: {name}
bitter_yuna_1.text: *I confessed. Yuna nodded, but her fingers continued to rub the end of the bookmark. About a month later, a note was placed in my locker. ‘Let’s talk.’*

bitter_yuna_2_library.name: Yuna
bitter_yuna_2_library.text: ...Sometimes I think of you. When I catch the scent of old books. I should've said more back then.

bitter_yuna_2_book.name: Yuna
bitter_yuna_2_book.text: ...Sometimes I think of you. When I pass a bookstore. I should've said more back then.

bitter_yuna_3.name: {name}
bitter_yuna_3.text: *I leave through the school gate. It's raining. In the mailbox, Yuna's last note is stuck. It's short. The bottom of the paper is smeared by rain.*

true_yuna_1.name: {name}
true_yuna_1.text: *The library annex. Deeper than the secret reading spot — an attic. A space I didn’t even know existed.*

true_yuna_2.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2.text: I was the only one who knew about this place.

true_yuna_2_b.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2_b.text: *She climbs the small attic ladder. There's a hatch leading up. — When it opens, a breeze rushes in.*

true_yuna_2_c.name: {name}
true_yuna_2_c.text: *Above the attic was the library annex rooftop. A secret passage no one else knows about.*

true_yuna_2_d.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2_d.text: *She leans against the railing. Stars are visible.*

true_yuna_3.name: Yuna
true_yuna_3.text: *She opens the small window. Stars are visible.*

true_yuna_5_b.name: Yuna
true_yuna_5_b.text: *Yuna pauses for a moment. The hand holding the book spine loosens.*

true_yuna_7.name: {name}
true_yuna_7.text: *Next to the third asterisk, a pale purple dot like the first note is marked. Yuna closes the notebook and walks toward the annex door first.*

true_yuna_bridge.name: {name}
true_yuna_bridge.text: *Yuna's stars are still here, right in front of me.*

true_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *Five days. That's how long it took to hear Yuna's voice beyond the notes.*

perfect_dain_1.name: {name}
perfect_dain_1.text: *The gym. Dain fires off her last serve. Unwrapping her bandages.*

perfect_dain_2.name: Dain
perfect_dain_2.text: This is the last toss. — But it's also the start of something.

perfect_dain_2b.name: Dain
perfect_dain_2b.text: *She sets the volleyball down and waits for {name}'s answer.*

perfect_dain_3.name: Dain
perfect_dain_3.text: Am I worth anything off the court too?

perfect_dain_3b.name: Dain
perfect_dain_3b.text: *She sets the volleyball down on the court. She turns and smiles. A quiet smile.*

perfect_dain_4.name: {name}
perfect_dain_4.text: On the court and off it.

perfect_dain_5.name: Dain
perfect_dain_5.text: *She threw herself at me before I was ready. The volleyball rolled across the floor, and in the sunset-lit gym, only our two shadows remained.*

perfect_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_dain.text: *Dain's knee buckles slightly as she lands from the jump. She laughs first, then presses her hand to her knee.*

perfect_epilogue_2_dain.name: Dain
perfect_epilogue_2_dain.text: *She became a sports commentator. Smiling in front of the camera too. This time, I don’t put emphasis on the end of my words.*

perfect_epilogue_3_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_3_dain.text: *Sometimes her knee hurts, she says. When it does, we sit side by side and listen to the air leak from the volleyball.*

bitter_dain_1.name: {name}
bitter_dain_1.text: *I confessed. Dain smiled good-naturedly. It was bright like gym lights, but it didn't last long. About a month later, I received a text message telling me to wait in front of the gym.*

bitter_dain_2.name: Dain
bitter_dain_2.text: It was fun! ...But I think it was only fun. That's what feels a little off.

bitter_dain_3.name: {name}
bitter_dain_3.text: *I leave the gym. Rain is falling. From behind the closed door, a ball bounces once.*

bitter_dain_3_b.name: {name}
bitter_dain_3_b.text: *I walked out past the school gate. It's raining. — No umbrella. Cherry blossoms stick to the wet ground at my feet.*

bitter_epilogue_1.name: {name}
bitter_epilogue_1.text: *After graduation, we heard from each other less and less. Once a month became once every two months, leaving each other on read became normal, and one day - when I opened the chat and had nothing to say - I knew it was over.*

bitter_epilogue_2.name: {name}
bitter_epilogue_2.text: *A record of five days remains. In the last photo, there's a gap between us wide enough for someone to walk through.*

true_dain_1.name: {name}
true_dain_1.text: *The gym. The same emergency lights as yesterday. Lying side by side on the mat.*

true_dain_2.name: Dain
true_dain_2.text: *She takes {name}'s hand and places it against the inside of her wrist. Without a word.*

true_dain_2b.name: {name}
true_dain_2b.text: *Fast. A speed that needs no words.*

true_dain_3.name: {name}
true_dain_3.text: *Her pulse beats clearly under my fingertips.*

true_dain_4.name: {name}
true_dain_4.text: *No words come out. My lips just go dry.*

true_dain_6.name: Dain
true_dain_6.text: *half hiding her face behind the volleyball* Why are you looking at me like that...? That's not fair.

true_dain_8.name: Dain
true_dain_8.text: You SO were!! ...But you can keep looking.

true_dain_8b.name: Dain
true_dain_8b.text: *The end of her voice lifts lightly. This time, it does not sound forced upward.*

true_dain_bridge.name: {name}
true_dain_bridge.text: *Dain's laughter still lingers in my ears.*

true_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_dain.text: *It was five days. Until I saw the moments when Dain could not smile.*

true_epilogue_2.name: {name}
true_epilogue_2.text: *The uniform was stiff, the cherry blossoms made me sneeze, and I had no idea what to do in front of the school gate.*

true_epilogue_3.name: {name}
true_epilogue_3.text: *But looking back — I think it was already decided the moment our eyes first met. It just took five days to admit it.*

true_epilogue_4_seo.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_seo.text: *Her mother's calls are still short, and the practice in front of the mirror isn't over. But Seoyeon sometimes looks my way with an unpracticed face now.*

true_epilogue_4_yuna.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_yuna.text: *Her senior's contact is still gone. The library corner seat is still empty. But Yuna now uses her voice before notes.*

true_epilogue_4_dain.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_dain.text: *Her knee is wrapped every morning. The alarm notes are still loud. Even so, Dain sometimes sends very short check-ins.*

day5_ending_alone.name: {name}
day5_ending_alone.text: *I walk out the school gate. My phone buzzes. — Nobody. Low battery warning.*

alone_1.name: {name}
alone_1.text: *Five days. On the desk sit a key, a note, and a wrist guard, side by side. I couldn't put any of them in my bag.*

alone_2.name: {name}
alone_2.text: *The room is quiet. On my phone screen, three chats are pinned at the top. None have new messages.*

alone_2_b.name: {name}
alone_2_b.text: *The room is quiet. Behind the sound of the door closing, voices fade away all at once. The cherry blossoms outside the window are scattered in the wind.*

alone_4.name: {name}
alone_4.text: *I turn off the room light and the notification sounds stop. Only the key, the note, and the wrist guard remain in the dark on the desk.*

day5_ending_good.name: {name}
day5_ending_good.text: *Just saying 'I like you' didn't magically fix everything. Even so, we chose not to end it here.*

good_1.name: {name}
good_1.text: *We were clumsy, late, and missed each other more than once.*

good_1b.name: {name}
good_1b.text: *Still, we walk in the same direction.*

good_1c.name: {name}
good_1c.text: *A cherry blossom petal sticks to the front of my shoe, then falls off on the next step.*

good_1_seo.name: Seoyeon
good_1_seo.text: We are both clumsy. ...But this time, do not let go halfway.

good_1_seo_b.name: Seoyeon
good_1_seo_b.text: *She brushes {name}'s sleeve once, as if removing a cherry blossom petal. The touch is blunt, but it is not pushing away.*

good_1_seo_c.name: Seoyeon
good_1_seo_c.text: *She silently falls half a step behind. She waits until {name}'s shoulder comes level with hers.*

good_1_seo_d.name: {name}
good_1_seo_d.text: *I walk side by side with Seoyeon. Our steps often fall out of sync, but neither lets go first.*

good_2_seo.name: {name}
good_2_seo.text: *At the end of the cherry blossom path, Seoyeon stops half a step ahead of me. When she looks back, her gaze is softer than it used to be.*

good_3_seo.name: {name}
good_3_seo.text: *"...Why aren't you coming?" She mutters it under her breath, but her slowed steps give her away — she was waiting.*

good_4_seo.name: {name}
good_4_seo.text: *I smile, and Seoyeon pretends not to see it before slowing her steps a little.*

good_5_seo.name: {name}
good_5_seo.text: *We walk slowly past the end of the cherry blossom road. This time, I do not swallow the words that I want to make another plan.*

good_epilogue_1.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1.text: *A text from Seoyeon. 'I made you a copy of the rooftop key. It's official, so don't worry.' She could've just called it an invitation.*

good_epilogue_2.name: Seoyeon
good_epilogue_2.text: *She never uses the word 'invitation' until the end. Instead, she sends a photo of the copied rooftop key.*

good_epilogue_3.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3.text: *I put the key in my pocket. Tomorrow, it is my turn to bring lunch to the rooftop.*

good_1_yuna.name: Yuna
good_1_yuna.text: ...You were late. Still — this time I read your sentence all the way to the end.

good_1_yuna_b.name: Yuna
good_1_yuna_b.text: *She hands me a folded note. When I open it, there's just one line: 'Next time, don't disappear.'*

good_1_yuna_b_b.name: {name}
good_1_yuna_b_b.text: *It's a short sentence, but this time it reads like a request.*

good_2_yuna.name: {name}
good_2_yuna.text: *The rooftop. Yuna leans against the railing. Even with the wind blowing, she doesn't turn away first today.*

good_3_yuna.name: {name}
good_3_yuna.text: *We look at the same sky. She doesn't say much, but the silence isn't cold the way it used to be.*

good_4_yuna.name: Yuna
good_4_yuna.text: *She slips the bookmark into a new page, on the side without a fold mark.*

good_5_yuna.name: {name}
good_5_yuna.text: *Go out the rooftop door and come down the stairs. The steps are slow but do not stop. This time, I will read to the end and speak to the end.*

good_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *A folded note falls from the bag. Creases mark where it was pressed against the lining for a long time. 'If you've finished volume 1, I'll lend you volume 2. — Yuna'*

good_epilogue_2_yuna.name: Yuna
good_epilogue_2_yuna.text: *Instead of words, she prepares what comes next. Volume 2 after volume 1. Tomorrow after today. This is her version of 'let's keep meeting.'*

good_epilogue_3_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3_yuna.text: *On the back of the note, in small writing: '...Let's read the ending together.' The pale violet ink is smeared.*

good_1_dain.name: Dain
good_1_dain.text: Hey, it's not like everything's fine yet. ...But I'm okay enough to throw you the ball again.

good_2_dain.name: {name}
good_2_dain.text: *In front of the school gate, Dain bounces the volleyball once and, this time without joking around, tosses it my way.*

good_3_dain.name: {name}
good_3_dain.text: *I catch it. Only then does Dain smile. The ball bounces once more in my palm.*

good_4_dain.name: {name}
good_4_dain.text: *My knee still has a bandage on it. Dain throws the ball, and I catch it a step too late.*

good_5_dain.name: {name}
good_5_dain.text: *We walk out through the school gate together. Dain loosens her wrist. This time, no ball comes over.*

good_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1_dain.text: *A message from Dain. 'Anyone wanna work out tomorrow morning?' There's a question mark at the end. Normally it'd be an exclamation point.*

good_epilogue_2_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_2_dain.text: *A short question stays on the screen for a long time.*

good_epilogue_3_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3_dain.text: *I texted back. 'Deal.' No exclamation mark. I'll show up in person tomorrow instead.*

day5_ending_confess_fail.name: {name}
day5_ending_confess_fail.text: *I told them. I said it. — But what came back was silence.*

confess_fail_cg_seo.name: {name}
confess_fail_cg_seo.text: *The screen stays still. The reply does not change.*

confess_fail_cg_yuna.name: {name}
confess_fail_cg_yuna.text: *The screen stays still. The reply does not change.*

confess_fail_cg_dain.name: {name}
confess_fail_cg_dain.text: *The screen stays still. The reply does not change.*

confess_fail_1.name: {name}
confess_fail_1.text: *Even after walking several steps away, I can't put the phone down. The last sentence remains beside the read mark.*

confess_fail_2.name: {name}
confess_fail_2.text: *I put my phone in my pocket and took it out again. The last sentence looked shorter next to the read mark.*

confess_fail_3.name: {name}
confess_fail_3.text: *I said it: I liked her. The reply took a long time to arrive, and it was short.*

confess_fail_4.name: {name}
confess_fail_4.text: *The words came out to the end. Maybe that is why my feet shake less when I turn away.*

day5_ending_friend.name: {name}
day5_ending_friend.text: *In the end, I couldn't say it.*

friend_1.name: {name}
friend_1.text: *The cherry blossoms are being blown away by the wind.*

friend_2.name: {name}
friend_2.text: *Same thing I did at my old school. I did it again.*

friend_3.name: {name}
friend_3.text: *There were moments I could have said I liked you. Each time, only a smile came out first.*

friend_4.name: {name}
friend_4.text: *I leave through the gate and there's a message on my phone. 'thanks for today lol' I type 'me too', then just add a smiley.*

friend_4_seo.name: {name}
friend_4_seo.text: *I leave through the gate and there's a message. 'Thanks to you it was less awkward today. Get home safe.' No emoji at the end of the sentence.*

friend_4_yuna.name: {name}
friend_4_yuna.text: *Walking out the school gate, a message arrives. '...Today. Thanks.' The cursor blinks after the period. No reply comes easily.*

friend_4_dain.name: {name}
friend_4_dain.text: *I leave through the gate and there's a message. 'Hey be careful! Thanks for today!' Two exclamation marks. I leave just 'ok' in the reply box.*

friend_5.name: {name}
friend_5.text: *I text back. 'Me too, thanks.' — Then stare at the screen. Two short lines. I'm smiling, but it doesn't feel good at all.*

friend_7.name: {name}
friend_7.text: *...I couldn’t say it at this school either.*

friend_8.name: {name}
friend_8.text: *Graduation day. Scrolling through my phone gallery. Where Sojeong's photo used to be three years ago, there's now a group photo with friends from this school. I'm turning my head away — just like I did back then.*

friend_9.name: {name}
friend_9.text: *Once again, I'm standing next to that person, wearing my easiest expression and smiling like just a friend.*

friend_10.name: {name}
friend_10.text: *I open the notes app. ‘I need to tell you something.’ — The cursor blinks. Just like three years ago. I hold down backspace and erase the words.*

day5_ending_mayhem.name: {name}
day5_ending_mayhem.text: *All three chats are stuck on 'read'. I try to write a reply, then delete it at the first letter.*

mayhem_1.name: Seoyeon
mayhem_1.text: *She passes {name} in the hallway. She does not turn her head.*

mayhem_2.name: {name}
mayhem_2.text: *Yuna’s seat was empty. A single note on the desk. ‘It was fun.’ The period was the end.*

mayhem_3.name: Dain
mayhem_3.text: *Dain laughed as usual. "how are you." The end of his words fell to the floor. There was no exclamation mark that I knew of.*

mayhem_4.name: {name}
mayhem_4.text: *I looked at the backs of the three people. None of the three turned around.*

mayhem_5.name: {name}
mayhem_5.text: *Spring is ending. The cherry blossoms are falling. No one is by my side.*

mayhem_6.name: {name}
mayhem_6.text: *The confirmation was sent, but every chat still held questions I hadn't answered.*

mayhem_7.name: {name}
mayhem_7.text: *Look at the unsent memo under Sojung’s photo. This time, the speech bubble sent was long. The screen turns dark as is.*

day5_ending_harem.name: {name}
day5_ending_harem.text: *I like all of you. — When those words left my mouth, all three faces froze at once.*

harem_1.name: Seoyeon
harem_1.text: *She laughed first....okay. That's honest. The laughter soon ended.*

harem_1_b.name: Yuna
harem_1_b.text: *She lowers her head. When she looks up much later, her fingertips are pressing hard into the book spine.*

harem_3.name: Dain
harem_3.text: *She hits {name}'s shoulder with her fist. It lands hard enough to sting. "Hey, you're the worst." There is no laughter at the end of the words.*

harem_4.name: {name}
harem_4.text: *Monday is Seoyeon. Wednesday is Yuna. Friday is Dain. Every time a calendar notification pops up, I flip the lock screen over first.*

harem_5.name: Seoyeon
harem_5.text: *When she asked, “What are you doing on Wednesday?”, his finger stopped in the reply window.*

harem_6.name: {name}
harem_6.text: *And still, all three of them are smiling today. Even knowing what tomorrow looks like, I reach for today again.*

harem_7.name: {name}
harem_7.text: *Three alarms go off at different times. Each time the vibrations overlap, the stomach reacts first.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_1.text: *Graduation is over. I'm alone in the empty classroom. The chalk marks on the blackboard haven't been erased yet.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_1b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_1b.text: *The door opens. — It's her. Beige cardigan. Holding a document envelope.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2.text: Congratulations on graduating. ...The paperwork's all done. My job as your teacher is finished now.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2b.text: Is the manuscript still in your desk drawer?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2c.text: *The teacher stops. The edge of the document envelope bends.* ...Take care.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3b.text: *Cafe terrace. Cherry blossoms drift through the air. As I step in - I see someone familiar at the window seat.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3c.text: ...Oh. I'm surprised too. *She sets down her coffee cup.* Want to sit?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3e.text: *She smirks.* Quit teaching. Just writing now. Part-time at a cafe too. — What about you?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3f.text: ...Can we meet again? I come here every Thursday.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3g.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3g.text: *The ‘next’ continued a few more times. Same spot every Thursday. When asked, ‘Is this a couple’s seat?’ both of them just looked down at their coffee. The next Thursday, I walked the streets instead of going to the cafe.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4b.text: *She stops suddenly at the bookstore.* ...I finished my manuscript. Want to read it?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4c.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4c.text: *I went home and read the manuscript. All night. — The main character's offhand lines kept sounding strangely familiar.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4d.text: *Next Thursday, at the café. She stirred her coffee longer than usual.* ...How was it?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4e.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4e.text: *Next Thursday. I didn't wait outside the cafe. — I waited outside the flower shop.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4f.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4f.text: *I hand over the bouquet.* On my side, it is just my feelings.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4g.text: *She takes the bouquet and stares at it for a long time. Her hands tremble. — She smiles.* ...Me neither.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_5.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_5.text: *As I was walking out the cafe door, the flower bouquet wrapper was a little crumpled in my hands. The diploma is in the bag.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep1.text: *We didn't leave the café that day. Not until sunset. The homeroom teacher sat for a long time with the cold coffee cup in front of her.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep2.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep2.text: *I was guided to the same spot every Thursday. Staff no longer ask, ‘Is this a couple’s seat?’*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep3.text: *The manuscript was published. No name in the dedication. Just one line: 'Three pages of feedback from the teacher's desk drawer — that's where this story began.'*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep4.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep4.text: *Sometimes, when I say, ‘I was a teacher,’ people respond with, ‘I was a student.’ They both laugh. That title doesn't stick around much longer.*

hidden_true_homeroom_1.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_1.text: *Graduation day. — Time has passed. The uniform isn't stiff anymore.*

hidden_true_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_2.text: *An empty classroom. The same classroom where she used to write. — My homeroom teacher is waiting.*

hidden_true_homeroom_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_2_b.text: *She's leaning by the window at the back of the classroom. No lessons, no duties — just her face.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4.text: ...Just now, you didn't call me teacher.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_4_b.text: *The way I addressed her feels unfamiliar a beat after it leaves my mouth.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_c.text: *The homeroom teacher takes out a white envelope. It is thinner than the brown envelope from last time.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_d.text: I finished the manuscript. — I could write it because you were my first reader.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_f.text: I asked for one line and you wrote three pages. After seeing that, I had no more excuses to postpone it.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_g.text: *She looks out the window. Cherry blossoms are falling.*

hidden_true_homeroom_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_5.text: *Looking out the window* ...So. Since I finished it, I'm thinking about sending it to a publisher. — What do you think?

hidden_true_homeroom_5_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_5_c.text: *The uniform isn't stiff anymore. No — today is the day I take it off.*

hidden_true_homeroom_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_6.text: ...Just one thing. ...Let's go get coffee. Real coffee this time, not juice.

hidden_true_homeroom_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_6_b.text: *The word coffee stays on the coaster for a long time.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_7_b.text: *The teacher smiles. Window light falls over the manuscript envelope.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_7_c.text: ...I really shouldn't be doing this. *— Her voice trails off. Then she smiles.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_7_d.text: *Her name lingers once more at the edge of my mouth. She smiles with her head turned away.*

hidden_true_homeroom_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_8.text: ...But even though I shouldn't be doing this — I don't regret it.

hidden_good_homeroom_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_good_homeroom_1.text: *She was waiting in front of the school.* Congratulations on graduating.

hidden_good_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_2.text: *During the handshake — something slips into my palm. A folded note.*

hidden_good_homeroom_3.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_3.text: *Leaving the school. 'When I finish the manuscript, I'll reach out. Because I want to show it to you first.' There's a phone number.*

hidden_good_homeroom_4.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_4.text: *Her hand held on about three seconds longer than a handshake should. Too long for a handshake, too short for a confession.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_1.text: *Graduation was over. I opened the nurse's office door. It was empty. A single bandage sat on the desk. 'Come to my place. Address on the back.' No heart this time.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_2.text: *The person who opened the door is wearing a knit instead of a gown.*...There you are. I really didn't think it would come.

hidden_perfect_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_3.text: *Side by side on the living room couch. The sun is setting outside the window. Instead of a bandage, fingers are touching.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_3b.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_3b.text: *Leaning on shoulder*...You don't have to make excuses anymore. Because I am neither a patient nor a student.

hidden_perfect_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_4.text: *Her hand rises to my tie, then lets go.* ...Stay a little longer today.

hidden_perfect_nurse_4b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_4b.text: *Morning. Light filters through the curtains. A bandage and a cold cup of coffee sit side by side on the table.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_5.text: *The school nurse opens her eyes and smiles.* ...Are you hurt? Want me to check? *She says it like a joke, but her fingertips are careful.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_5b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_5b.text: *I don’t want to take my hand away. Here.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep1.text: *Morning. A bandage is stuck to the dining table. Today's menu is written on it in tiny letters.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep2.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep2.text: *She returned to the university hospital. Patients call her by name. — Nurse Lee Juwon.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep3.text: *The rosemary pot has been moved to the windowsill. To the sunny side. — She's watering it.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep4.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep4.text: *The light green notebook went deep into the drawer. One line remains near the bottom of the last page. 'Yujin, I'm okay now.'*

hidden_true_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_1.text: *Graduation day. Walking out the school gate — there's a bandage stuck to the nurse's office door.*

hidden_true_nurse_2.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2.text: *'Congrats on graduating. I'll be waiting at the café.' Peeling off the bandage reveals a small map inside. By the café window seat, two cold coffees sit in front of the nurse.*

hidden_true_nurse_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2_b.text: *There is no gown or attendance register today.*

hidden_true_nurse_3.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_3.text: Congrats on graduating. Starting today, you can drop the 'teacher.'

hidden_true_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_4.text: You know... when you came to the nurse's office on your first day. You touched your forehead and asked if I could 'check your blood pressure that way.' I thought you were joking.

hidden_true_nurse_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5.text: ...But right now, I don't intend to gloss over it like that.

hidden_true_nurse_5_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_5_b.text: *The hand holding the coffee cup stops. There was no room for jokes to escape.*

hidden_true_nurse_5_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_c.text: I knew it couldn't be, right? That's why I kept passing it off as a joke.

hidden_true_nurse_5_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_d.text: But you saw right through me, even when I was glossing things over.

hidden_true_nurse_5_e.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_5_e.text: Taking three minutes to put on a bandage isn't just being careful.

hidden_true_nurse_5_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_f.text: *The nurse sets down her coffee cup. Her smile arrives a little late.*

hidden_true_nurse_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_6.text: So after the ceremony — come see me again. Not at the nurse's office. Here. And next time, I'll be just Juwon, not the school nurse.

hidden_true_nurse_7.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_7.text: *Even after we left the cafe, our hands didn't part easily. By the time I came to my senses, we were standing in front of her house, not the nurse's office.*

hidden_true_nurse_7_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_7_b.text: ...I see you've been watching that far.

hidden_true_nurse_7_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_7_c.text: *The school nurse reaches out and touches the bandage on the back of {name}'s hand. It is the one she put on that morning.*

hidden_true_nurse_7_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_7_d.text: *The nurse presses the edge of the bandage once with her nail, then lets go.*

hidden_true_nurse_8.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8.text: Now, don't pretend to be hurt just to come see me. Just say you wanted to see me.

hidden_true_nurse_8_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_b.text: *Turning her coffee cup in her hands* ...I never thought I'd miss the smell of the nurse's office after graduation.

hidden_true_nurse_8_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_c.text: *For a moment, the white curtain of the nurse’s office overlaps the cafe window, then disappears.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_d.text: *The hand that was turning the coffee cup stops.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_e.text: You know... back then, I was thinking about quitting.

hidden_true_nurse_8_g.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_g.text: But when you came — I had a reason to stay here. *Smiling softly* Thank you.

hidden_good_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2.text: Vitamins. — Take care of your health in college. ...Let's call it medical concern.

hidden_good_nurse_2_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2_c.text: *Pausing for a moment* ...Right. Medical concern. *quietly* Let's leave it at that.

hidden_good_nurse_2_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2_d.text: *The nurse rubs the bottle label with her thumb. Her smile follows a little late.*

hidden_good_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_3.text: *Leaving the nurse's office. Inside the bottle cap, tiny writing. 'Call me if you're sick. Call me even if you're not. — ♥'*

hidden_good_nurse_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_3_b.text: *Even after I close the cap, the corners of my mouth won't go down.*

hidden_good_nurse_4.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_4.text: *My hand stops around the bottle. The drawer that held the light green notebook is closed.*

perfect_epilogue_1b_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1b_dain.text: *Every morning wrapping bandages, secretly rubbing her knee when no one was looking. That person just jumped.*

perfect_epilogue_1c_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1c_dain.text: *On days when his knees hurt, Dain slows down. I beat to the same beat next to him.*
